To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the variation of circulating VEGF and TGF-beta 1 is largely attributable to genetic factors and (2) the genetic influences are the major (or the sole) source for the covariations of VEGF and TIMP-1, and TGF-beta1 and TIMP- 1.
(1) the plasma levels of VEGF and TGF-beta 1 are highly heritable, and (2) the genetic and environmental factors influencing these molecules are shared with EGF and TIMP-1.

the circulating levels of growth factors involved in angiogenesis are determined by both genetic and environmental factors; the genetic effects are the major source of phenotypic correlations between these molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first quantitative genetic analysis of the circulating variation in growth factors (VEFG, EGF, TGF-beta1, TIMP-1) involved in angiogenic processes in a large sample of Caucasian healthy families.
the genetic architecture of circulating growth factors, which are involved in the angiogenic processes.
the genetic and environmental influences that determine the circulating levels of VEGF, EGF and TGF-beta 1 in a population of healthy individuals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

genetic factors are the primary determinant of the populational variation in circulating levels of the VEGF, EGF, TGF-beta 1 and TIMP-1, with the remaining variation being due to common environmental effects.

the variation of these molecules is under the control of a complex genetic system, in which the pleiotropic effects of a small number of genes are the primary (or sole) determinants of the phenotypic correlations between the molecules.

the circulating levels of these growth factors are under strong genetic control, and that their phenotypic correlations are primarily attributable to the pleiotropic effects of the same or closely linked genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the variation in the levels of these growth factors is largely due to the additive effects of genetic factors, which are shared to a large extent with the variation in other molecules involved in the angiogenic process.

the genetic factors are the main determinants of the variation of VEGF, EGF and their covariations with TGF-beta 1 or TIMP-1, while the environmental factors also contribute to the variation in the levels of these molecules.
genetic and environmental factors, both shared and non-shared, are important in the determination of the variation of the studied molecules in the population.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the genetic effects are of primary importance for the populational variation in circulating levels of growth factors, which may be useful in identifying individuals at risk of angiogenesis-related diseases and in developing more targeted and effective therapies.

the genetic factors are a major determinant of circulating VEGF, EGF, TIMP-1 and TGF-beta 1 levels, thus suggesting that these molecules may be used as potential biomarkers in genetic studies of angiogenesis.
the circulating variation of the studied angiogenic factors is largely determined by genetic factors, which may be of interest in the search for novel genetic markers for angiogenesis.
